determinism_anomaly_status.probe_result: the probe did not reproduce the 192-token rep1 text: with the production flags all five decision_contract occurrences (stream, non-stream, after 4 filler tasks) gave the 188-token rep0 text. With --ctx-checkpoints 0 all five gave a third text (198 tokens, differs in the goal and reason strings). So the output depends on the server's prompt-processing layout: with checkpoints enabled the prompt is split into ubatches at the message boundaries where checkpoints are created (19 / 231 tokens in the trace), without checkpoints it is processed in plain 1024-token ubatches, and the two layouts give slightly different logits that flip near-tie tokens.
determinism_anomaly_status.why_rep1_was_not_reproduced: bench_spec runs 8 tasks per rep; the probe ran only 4 fillers, so the slot/checkpoint state before the second occurrence differed (the stored trace of spec_off shows rep1 resuming from a restored checkpoint at n_past = 54, i.e. yet another layout).
determinism_anomaly_status.ctx_control_observation: with --cache-ram 0 --ctx-checkpoints 0 (full recompute every call) the same A prompt gave a different 48-token output in 6 of 30 occurrences across the 2x3 (rep,size) sequences (e.g. 30k rep1 B_repeat differs from A_fresh immediately before it). That is run-to-run, same-layout variation and is not explained by layout alone.
determinism_anomaly_status.next: determinism_probe2: (1) same prompt, no cache/checkpoints, -ub 1024/512/256, 3 calls each with top-3 logprobs -> does the output follow the ubatch layout and is it stable within a layout; (2) exact bench_spec order replay under production flags with the server trace -> reproduce 192 and read the first divergent token margin.
